name: STM8S003F3P6TR
title: STM8S003F3/K3 value line 8-bit MCU: 16 MHz STM8 core, 8 Kbytes Flash, 128 bytes data EEPROM, three timers, 10-bit ADC, UART, SPI and I2C
summary: STM8S003F3 and STM8S003K3 are value-line 8-bit microcontrollers built on the 16 MHz STM8 core, with 8 Kbytes Flash, 1 Kbyte RAM and 128 bytes of data EEPROM, working from 2.95 V to 5.5 V. They carry a 16-bit advanced-control timer, a 16-bit general-purpose timer, an 8-bit timer, UART, SPI, I2C, a 10-bit ADC with up to 5 inputs, window and independent watchdogs, auto-wakeup and a beeper, clocked from internal 16 MHz and 128 kHz RC oscillators or an external crystal. The F3 comes in TSSOP20 and UFQFPN20 with 16 I/Os, the K3 in LQFP32 with 28; STM8S003F3P6TR is the TSSOP20 part for -40 °C to 85 °C on tape and reel.

STM8S003F3 pin description (TSSOP20, UFQFPN20)
rows: Top level interrupt [AFR3]; Timer 1 - inverted channel 1 [AFR7]
notes: Type column: I/O marks signal pins, S marks supply pins.
Input level is CMOS on every I/O. HS marks a high-sink output.
Output speed: O1 is slow (2 MHz max); O2 is fast (10 MHz max); O3 and O4 switch between the two, starting slow (O3) or fast (O4) after reset.

Input columns: floating, wpu (weak pull-up), external interrupt. Output columns: OD (open-drain capable), PP (push-pull capable); T in the OD column is a true open drain with no P-buffer, weak pull-up or protection diode to VDD.
X (reset) marks the configuration the pin takes after the internal reset is released; unless noted it holds during reset too. PD1/SWIM is pulled up both during reset and after it.

Square brackets name an alternate function reached through an AFR option bit; the default alternate function is then lost. A function listed twice on different pins is a choice of one pin, not two copies.
Pins driving or sinking high current at the same time are to be spread evenly around the package, and the total current stays within the absolute maximum ratings.
In halt and active-halt, PA1 turns into an input with weak pull-up, is not driven and cannot wake the device; with those modes in use PA1 serves best as an input.

rows: Input voltage on true open drain pins(2)
Input voltage on any other pin(2)
Variations between all the different ground pins
notes: (1) Every VDD and VSS pin is connected to the supply.

(2) Keeping VIN within its limits keeps the injected current within IINJ(PIN); otherwise the current is limited externally. VIN above VDD injects positive current, VIN below VSS negative. True open-drain pins take no positive injection, so their VIN maximum always applies.
Stress beyond these ratings can damage the device; operation at them is not implied, and long exposure can reduce reliability. The mission profile follows JEDEC JESD47.

notes: (1) From characterization.
(2) Every VDD and VSS pin is connected to the supply.
(3) Keeping VIN within its limits keeps IINJ(PIN) within its rating; otherwise limit the current externally. True open-drain pins take no positive injection.

(4) Negative current injected into one analog input degrades the conversion on another analog input; a Schottky diode from such a pin to ground is recommended. Positive injection within the IINJ(PIN) and ΣIINJ(PIN) limits leaves ADC accuracy unchanged.
(5) With several pins injected at once, ΣIINJ(PIN) adds the magnitudes of the positive and negative instantaneous currents; characterized with the maximum total spread over four I/O pins.

circuits.title: Recommended reset pin protection
circuits.description: NRST carries a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground; an external reset source may drive the same node. The internal pull-up RPU charges the capacitor, which keeps short disturbances from resetting the device.

parts.note: 10 nF at least; a smaller value cuts charge and discharge current

notes: The external reset source has to pull NRST below VIL max, or the reset is not seen inside.
When NRST also resets other parts, the capacitor's charge and discharge time sets the reset pulse they get.

circuits.title: Typical application with I2C bus
circuits.description: Both I2C lines are pulled up to VDD with 4.7 kΩ on the bus side and reach the SDA and SCL pins through 100 Ω series resistors.

circuits.title: Typical application with ADC
circuits.description: A source VAIN feeds an analog input AINx through its series resistance RAIN, with the stray capacitance CAIN from the pin to ground. Inside, the pin has clamp diodes to VDD and ground (VT 0.6 V), a leakage of ±1 µA and the 3 pF sample-and-hold capacitor CADC.

parts.note: below 10 kΩ for the ADC accuracy figures

notes: The source resistance has to let the input capacitance (3 pF max) settle within the sampling time tS.

circuits.title: HSE oscillator circuit
circuits.description: A crystal or ceramic resonator between OSCIN and OSCOUT with a load capacitor from each pin to ground. The amplifier and the feedback resistor RF (220 kΩ typ) are inside the chip.

parts.note: CL1 = CL2 = C, 20 pF max recommended; C is about twice the crystal load capacitance

notes: Resonator and load capacitors go as close to the oscillator pins as possible, which limits output distortion and start-up time.
Start-up needs gm well above gmcrit.

circuits.title: HSE external clock source
circuits.description: An external clock drives OSCIN directly, between VHSEL and VHSEH, at up to 16 MHz; option bit EXTCLK selects this mode.

operation.text: STM8S003F3 (20 pins) and STM8S003K3 (32 pins) are value-line STM8S parts with 8 Kbytes Flash, 1 Kbyte RAM and 128 bytes of true data EEPROM rated for 100 000 write/erase cycles; they are low-density devices of the STM8S family. Watchdogs, internal oscillators and brown-out reset are on chip.

8-bit STM8 core, Harvard architecture, 3-stage pipeline, 32-bit program memory bus so most instructions fetch in one cycle. Registers: 8-bit accumulator, 16-bit X and Y index registers, 24-bit program counter (16-Mbyte linear space), 16-bit stack pointer (64 K-level stack) and an 8-bit CC register holding 7 flags. 20 addressing modes, including indexed indirect and stack-pointer relative; 80 instructions averaging 2 bytes, with 8 x 8 multiply, 16/8 and 16/16 divide and bit manipulation.

The single-wire interface module on PD1/SWIM gives in-circuit programming and non-intrusive real-time debugging in every operating mode, at up to 145 byte/ms. The debug module reads and writes RAM and peripheral registers on the fly, can stall the CPU to reach everything, supports software breakpoints on any program instruction and two advanced breakpoints with 23 predefined configurations, and follows CPU operation through shadow registers.

Nested interrupt controller with three software priority levels and 32 hardware-prioritised vectors. Up to 27 external interrupt lines share six vectors, the top-level interrupt TLI among them. Trap and reset complete the set.

The memory access security system (MASS) always write-protects program Flash, data EEPROM and option bytes; writing the MASS key sequence to a control register opens them for in-application programming. A second level, the user boot code (UBC) area, is set by option byte OPT1 in steps of one 64-byte page and stays locked during IAP even after the MASS keys. It suits boot code, libraries, the reset and interrupt vectors and IAP routines. Program memory is the 8 Kbytes minus the UBC area.

With ROP enabled (OPT0 = 0xAA) the Flash and data EEPROM can be neither read nor written in ICP or debug mode. Any attempt to change the ROP state erases the program memory. ROP can only be changed in ICP mode through SWIM.

Four master clock sources: 1 to 16 MHz crystal (HSE), up to 16 MHz external clock on OSCIN, the 16 MHz internal RC (HSI, user-trimmable) and the 128 kHz internal RC (LSI). After reset the device runs from HSI/8, 2 MHz. A prescaler trades speed against current; sources switch on the fly without glitches, the switch waiting until the new source is ready. Clocks to the core, to individual peripherals and to memory can be gated off. The clock security system, when enabled, falls back to HSI/8 on an HSE failure and can raise an interrupt. CCO outputs a clock on a pin.

Wait: CPU stopped, peripherals running; any interrupt or reset wakes it. Active halt with regulator on: CPU and peripheral clocks stopped, the AWU wakes the device at programmed intervals; faster wakeup, higher current. Active halt with regulator off: as before with the main regulator off, slower wakeup. Halt: lowest current, CPU and peripheral clocks and main regulator off; an external event or reset wakes it.

Two independent watchdogs, each started by option byte or by software and then impossible to stop short of a reset. The window watchdog resets on time-out (75 µs to 64 ms at 16 MHz) or when refreshed before the counter has dropped below the window value. The independent watchdog runs from the 128 kHz LSI, so it keeps going if the CPU clock fails; its period spans 60 µs to 1 s.

The AWU wakes the device from active halt, clocked by the LSI or by the external clock; the LSI can be routed to TIM1 input capture channel 1 to calibrate it. The beeper drives the BEEP pin at 1, 2 or 4 kHz; the BEEP output is reached only through remap option bit AFR7.

16-bit advanced-control timer: up, down and up/down auto-reload counter with a 16-bit prescaler; four capture/compare channels for input capture, output compare, edge- or centre-aligned PWM and one-pulse mode; three complementary outputs whose dead time can be set; break input forcing the outputs to a set state; synchronisation with external signals; encoder mode. Suits motor control, lighting and half-bridge drive. Interrupts: 3 capture/compare, 1 update/overflow, 1 break.

TIM2: 16-bit auto-reload up-counter, prescaler of any power of 2 from 1 to 32768, three capture/compare channels, PWM; interrupts for 3 capture/compare and 1 update/overflow. TIM4: 8-bit auto-reload, prescaler of any power of 2 from 1 to 128, clocked from the CPU clock, one update/overflow interrupt.

10-bit successive-approximation converter with up to 5 multiplexed external inputs, range 0 to VDDA, 14 clock cycles per conversion. Single, continuous and buffered continuous modes with a 10 x 10-bit buffer; scan of a channel sequence; analog watchdog with upper and lower thresholds and an interrupt; external trigger input and trigger from TIM1 TRGO; end-of-conversion interrupt. Input AIN12 cannot be used in scan mode or with the analog watchdog, and its results go only to ADC_DRH/ADC_DRL.

Full-duplex UART up to 1 Mbit/s (fCPU/16) with a high-precision baud-rate generator that reaches any standard rate whatever the input clock, separate transmitter and receiver enables, address-bit and idle-line wakeup, parity and error interrupts. Also synchronous mode with clock output as an SPI master (8-bit, up to 1 Mbit/s at 16 MHz), SmartCard, IrDA SIR, single-wire half duplex and LIN master (sends a 13-bit break, detects an 11-bit break).

Up to 8 Mbit/s (fMASTER/2) as master or slave, full duplex, or simplex on two lines with a bidirectional data line. Master or slave chosen by hardware or software; CRC calculation; one-byte transmit and receive buffers; slave-select input pin.
Master (clock, start and stop generation) and slave (programmable address detection, stop detection); 7-bit and 10-bit addressing and general call; standard mode to 100 kHz and fast mode to 400 kHz.

Eight AFR option bits move some alternate functions to other pins; with a remap active the default alternate function is gone. A peripheral's alternate function works only once the peripheral is enabled. Remapping leaves the GPIO behaviour of the pins unchanged.

Option bytes set hardware features and memory protection and live in their own memory block at 0x4800. Each one except ROP is stored twice, plain (OPTx) and complemented (NOPTx). They are written in ICP mode through SWIM, or on the fly by running firmware (IAP); ROP alone needs ICP.

Voltages refer to VSS. Min and max values hold over the worst temperature, supply and frequency and are production-tested at TA = 25 °C and TA max; values marked as from characterization are mean ± 3 sigma of samples and not tested. Typical values (TA = 25 °C, VDD = 5 V) are guidance and untested. The typical ADC accuracy figures cover 95 % of a lot (mean ± 2 sigma) over the full temperature range. Typical curves are guidance only.

VDD runs from 2.95 V to 5.5 V; every VDD and VSS pin is tied to the supply. The main 1.8 V regulator is stabilised by CEXT on VCAP: 470 nF to 3300 nF, ESR at most 0.3 Ω and ESL at most 15 nH at 1 MHz, over the capacitor's full tolerance, temperature, bias and frequency range.

The power-on/brown-out reset is always active. VDD rises above VIT+ (2.6 to 2.85 V) to leave reset after up to 1.7 ms (tTEMP) and falls below VIT- (2.5 to 2.8 V) to enter it; hysteresis is 70 mV typ. VDD slew rates of 2 µs/V or slower in either direction are allowed.

Supply currents are measured with every I/O an input held statically at VDD or VSS without load and every peripheral clock off unless named. The typical current curves are taken with code running from RAM.

The HSE takes a 1 to 16 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator. Its figures come from characterization with typical external parts. Resonator and load capacitors sit as close as possible to OSCIN and OSCOUT.

Unused pins are held at a fixed level, by driving them as outputs or through an external resistor to either rail. The weak pull-up behaves as a pure resistor: its current extrapolates linearly to zero at 0 V. Output level curves are taken with one pin loaded.

NRST has a 30 to 80 kΩ pull-up and a filter that ignores pulses up to 75 ns and passes 500 ns and longer. A capacitor of at least 10 nF (0.1 µF in the recommended network) guards against spurious resets. An external reset source has to pull NRST below VIL max. When NRST also resets other parts, the capacitor's charge and discharge time sets their reset pulse.

Negative current injected into an analog input upsets conversions on other inputs; a Schottky diode from such a pin to ground is recommended. Positive injection within the IINJ(PIN) and ΣIINJ(PIN) limits does not change accuracy.

ESD (IEC 61000-4-2) and fast transient bursts through 100 pF on VDD and VSS (IEC 61000-4-4) are applied while the part toggles two LEDs, until it fails; a reset restores normal operation. Software should handle a corrupted program counter, unexpected resets and corrupted control registers. Most such failures are recovered by holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 second.
The order code carries the temperature range; suffix 6 is -40 to 85 °C ambient with junction up to 105 °C. TJmax follows from the application's dissipation and the package ΘJA.
